Alex: FYI planning rolling soft-reboots + kernel driver refresh in euc1 tomorrow 00:30-02:30 UTC. Target: pool-euc1-D, ~10 racks (~80 GPUs). Sequence: 2-rack batches, short warmback.
Rina: Ack. What's our acceptable latency uplift?
Alex: Keep p95 <= 240ms generally. Emergency cap p95 <= 450ms only for background/noncritical routes. Critical routes must stay <900ms.
Tom: Capacity math: expecting ~35% spill -> ~28 GPUs. With 25% warm buffer -> need ~35 GPUs hot. If we use us-central dedicated as fallback cost ~ $900/hr.
Jules: eu-central has a brief maintenance 01:45-02:15 UTC, might lose ~6 GPUs then. Avoid flow to eu-central after 01:30.
Alex: Plan: pre-seed KV at 23:50, synthetic replay at 00:10, start drains 00:30. Pause every 2 racks for 7m observation. If p95 > 380ms stop.
Rina: Add metric evac_spill_gpus and alert if >45 -> auto-pause drain. Also emit route_shift_pct.
Tom: Draining command (dry): `ops drain --pool=pool-euc1-D --batch=2 --grace=100` plus kubectl drain per node.
Jules: Routing: primary fallback dedicated-us-central, secondary us-west3 (only before 01:30). Tag noninteractive routes for -25% rate limit.
Alex: Rollback triggers: evac_spill_gpus>45, p95>380ms for 5m, or >2 pod eviction errors. Rollback action: `ops rollback-drain --restore-weights`.
Rina: I'll update status page and customer comms.
Tom: I'll stage seed & replay jobs and post node list in runbook.
ops-bot: Scheduled: maintenance-window: euc1 2025-10-11T00:30Z-02:30Z by Alex. Ticket: MW-3892. Runbook PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/920.
Alex: Thanks all. Will post go/no-go 45m prior.
